scope_and_caveats: SEMI-SYNTHETIC: integer-sum Viterbi lattice (the algorithm's home turf, heavy position x time merging) + an oracle-defined competence generator. NOT a real LM.

The strong positive is lattice-only. The real-Phi confirm cells stay negative/null: Countdown D1_exec -0.083 at effective depth ~3 (builtin_small is 4-number = 3 ops; the D4 lattice cell is ALSO null/zero, so this is consistent with 'advantage needs depth', not a contradiction), algebra null (mock step-generator is the binding constraint). A real domain with a CHEAP solvability oracle and DEEP horizon is needed for real-domain confirmation; countdown.reachable is exponential and caps depth ~5.

synthesis.claim_under_test: On the honest moves/exec axis, with a freq (and verifier-masked) headline arm and adequate beam, global decode beats compute-matched selection, and the margin GROWS with horizon depth.
why_no: MATERIAL BUG (controlling): the fair generator memoizes good/bad classification AND seeds its RNG by canon(state)=(s,r), which omits the per-instance target T. One generator is built per (depth,K,p,seed) cell (run_mechanism2._run_cell line 173) and shared across all 24 instances, which have different T but overlapping (s,r) canons. The first instance to touch an (s,r) fixes weights+seed under the WRONG T for all later instances. solvable-based classification depends on T, so savi_freq is biased downward. Every pass@1 / D1_exec / D_verif / D_merge in outputs/lattice_sweep/results2.json came from this contaminated path (reproduced bit-for-bit by the verifier). The sweep must be re-run with a per-instance generator (or canon=(s,r,T)) and the current cache.json deleted before any conclusion.

DEPTH SUB-CLAIM FALSE even in the contaminated data: D1_exec is non-monotone in depth in every (K,p) slice (rises to a D16 peak then DECAYS at D24; negative and worsening at K=8 for D>=8). Beam width K, not depth, gates the sign. 'Margin grows with depth' is not what the data show.

Published numbers are biased strongly downward.
